$description: The glyphs a part draws where a renderer has cells rather than pixels (a terminal), each with a Unicode form and an ASCII form, and the icons, each with a Nerd Font form (typeface-terminal names a Nerd Font face) and the same two fallbacks. A part lists what it draws in its `cells.glyphs`. Every Unicode form here is one cell wide where a terminal draws East Asian ambiguous characters narrow, as terminals do by default; a renderer measures widths and never counts characters, and takes the ASCII forms in a terminal that cannot show the Unicode ones.
rules: Unicode by default; ASCII where the terminal's character set or the reader asks for it; an icon's Nerd Font form only where the reader says the face is there, since a terminal cannot choose its font.
An icon beside its own word (Try again, a menu item's label) may be left out in ASCII; an icon alone (an icon button, a mark) takes its ASCII form, and its name is said in the status line on focus.
Without color, a state is carried by its glyph and its words (index.json, colorDepth.none): the sort arrows, the check, the status dot beside a state's word, the issue mark.
No glyph here is one an emoji font may draw two cells wide.

sortable.means: A sortable column that is not sorted, where a part shows it (table head, on focus).

chevron-right.means: Between crumbs of a trail, a submenu, a row that opens.

chevron-left.means: Back (the top bar's last crumb below md, the page header's back).

chevron-down.means: A select's trigger; an open group.

spinner.means: Busy or loading, in an icon's place: one frame each motion-fast; the first frame alone where motion is stilled.

status-dot.means: A state's dot before its word, the status line's live dot, an unread dot.

bullet.means: Before each item of a list of problems.

missing.means: A value that is not there, in a quiet ink (principle 10).

ellipsis.means: Text cut short at its end.

check.means: The chosen row of a select, a checked menu item.

checkbox-off.means: A row not selected (table's select column).

focus-mark.means: The active entry's bar (rail), and keyboard focus on a row of a table or a list: in ring at the row's start (open questions, T4).

rule.means: A rule across: under a head, over the foot, between groups.

rule-heavy.means: A heavy rule across: a critical section's top line, which the web draws as a 2px critical rule over the box.

grid-dot.means: A dot of the graph tone's dot grid (a section's ground in the graph tone), in the grid's ink, one every few cells.

edge-start.means: A one-row control's edge at its start (a button, a field's control, a select's trigger): in the edge's flat color, inside the padding, the ground keeping its width (open questions, T3).

edge-end.means: A one-row control's edge at its end, as edge-start.

focus-ring-start.means: Keyboard focus on a one-row control: in ring, in the cell before its start, outside its width, in the gap its cells keep between controls (open questions, T4).

focus-ring-end.means: Keyboard focus on a one-row control: in ring, in the cell after its end, as focus-ring-start.

scroll-thumb.means: A scroller's thumb, in its own column (scrollbar-width keeps the room).

mask.means: One character of a masked value (a secret field's input while hidden, a sealed secret's dots): one cell each, the value never on screen.

spark-levels.means: A sparkline's eight levels, lowest first: each value one cell, at the level its share of the line's range gives it, in the reading's color (stat-panel's spark, a stat's trend).

stale.means: A panel's or a tile's stale mark: its data is older than it should be (dashboard-panel, stat-panel), its words in the status line on focus.

swatch.means: A series' or a value's color in a legend (a chart's legend, a threshold legend), in that color.

rule-start.means: A rule down a block's start, in each of its rows' first column: a problem's 2px rule in its tone.

box.$description: Box corners and sides. The radius ladder is one bit in cells: a corner role above 0 draws rounded, 0 square.

icons.$description: By the Lucide name sokkel-ui draws, kebab-cased. `nerdFont` is the codicon's codepoint in Nerd Fonts (its name in `nerdFontName`). Each name and codepoint is the one Nerd Fonts publishes, checked against vendor/nerd-fonts.json (scripts/nerd-fonts.py).

loader.note: Drawn as the spinner glyph's frames wherever it turns; this form is its still frame.
